title: Inference metric relay and resilient OTLP fallback for per-customer KPIs
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a resilient metric relay that unifies Prometheus scrape metrics and OTLP metric streams from the inference runtime, enriches them with routing/model/context labels, and provides a fallback path when direct scraping fails. This aims to improve per-customer and per-model P95/P99 latency KPIs, make SLI derivation deterministic, and reduce missing-series incidents during transient control-plane failures.

Scope:
- Metric relay service running in each region that accepts: (1) Prometheus remote_write from scrape targets, (2) OTLP metric streams from runtime sidecars, and (3) batched edge-aggregated summaries from inference nodes.
- Normalization/enrichment pipeline: attach model_id, deployment_stage, route_id, shard_id, customer_tier, and sampling_key.
- Local aggregation for short-window percentiles (1s/10s) to reduce cardinality and cost.
- Guaranteed fallback: if Prometheus scrapes fail, runtime sidecars switch to OTLP push with prefixed labels and TTL; relay deduplicates and stitches series.
- Backpressure and circuit breaker: protect the relay from bursts and fall back to compressed, delta-encoded summaries.
- Deterministic sampling for high-cardinality debug metrics with an injected sample seed per request to allow reconstruction when needed.
- Export targets: central OTLP ingestion, Prometheus long-term adapter, and a per-project short-term Redis cache for rapid SLO lookups.

Non-goals: building UI dashboards in this ticket (dashboard links provided), changing model-serving metric names, or replacing the long-term metrics store.

Success metrics:
- Reduce missing-series incidents impacting latency dashboards by >=90% in the next release window.
- 30% reduction in per-token metric egress for high-cardinality models via local aggregation and label normalization.
- Deterministic SLI derivation enabling identical P95 numbers between Canary and Production within 0.5% deviation.
acceptance_criteria: Relay service deployed to two staging regions and one canary production cell
Prometheus remote_write and OTLP streams are both accepted and merged without duplicate double-counting
Model/model-version label attached to >=99% of inference metric series
Fallback path audited in a chaos run: simulate scrape timeout and verify OTLP push succeeds and dashboards show continuous data
Documented config for sampling rate and aggregation window in Confluence

2025-02-18 - Connor Li: Design doc drafted; choosing OTLP as canonical wire format to simplify relay logic and avoid Prometheus label explosion. Posting PR with proto changes (see links).

2025-02-25 - Elena Park (Design): Reviewed enrichment fields; request to add customer_tier and anonymized customer_hash for billing alignment. Agreed to append hashed_customer_id instead of raw tenant ids.

2025-02-27 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Raised capacity concerns for short-window percentile computation at scale. Decided to implement local t-digest summarization with configurable precision to trade accuracy for CPU.
2025-03-01 - Connor Li: Implemented initial relay binary and canary manifests. Deployed to staging-1. Observed 18% reduction in metric egress for top-3 models due to local aggregation. Open PR: #4123

2025-03-03 - QA: Performed fallback chaos test by introducing 5s scrape delays. Relay accepted OTLP pushes and Grafana dashboards showed continuous series; need to add alerting for relay queue saturation.
2025-03-05 - Aisha Raman: Updated acceptance criteria to require documented sampling strategy and added due date to align with telemetry-2025.03 release planning.
